title: Chicago-Style Deep-Dish Cheese Pizza with Buttery Crust and Chunky Tomato
summary: A tall, buttery cornmeal crust filled with a thick layer of mozzarella, chunky garlic and basil tomato sauce and a dusting of Parmesan. Rich, generous and best eaten with a knife and fork.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook, or a large bowl
two 23 cm round metal cake tins, at least 4 cm deep (dark metal browns best; not loose-based)
cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
canned whole peeled plum tomatoes (no added salt; 2 cans)
fine sea salt or table salt
low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella, sliced 3 mm thick (or coarsely grated)

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, cornmeal, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water and melted butter and knead on medium, or by hand, for 5 minutes until smooth and glossy. Cover and leave for 1 hour, until nearly doubled. The cornmeal adds a slight crunch and golden colour to the crust.

steps.title: Cook the chunky sauce
steps.text: While the dough rises, drain the tomatoes in the sieve for 10 minutes and crush them roughly by hand. Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat and cook the grated onion and oregano for 5 minutes, until the liquid has gone and the onion is golden. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes, salt and sugar, and simmer briskly for 25-30 minutes, stirring often, until thick, chunky and reduced to about 600ml.

steps.title: Cool the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the basil and leave the sauce to cool. A thick, cooled sauce stops the deep crust from going soggy during the long bake.

steps.title: Laminate with butter
steps.text: Roll the dough on an unfloured surface into a 38 x 30cm rectangle and spread the very soft butter over it, leaving a 1cm border. Roll it up tightly from a short side, flatten the roll into a long strip, cut it in half crosswise, then fold each half in three and pinch into a ball. Cover and chill for 40 minutes; the thin butter layers create a flaky, biscuit-like crust.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Set a shelf in the lowest position and heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C) for at least 20 minutes before baking. Baking low ensures the base of the deep tin gets enough heat to brown.

steps.title: Line the tins
steps.text: Oil each tin with 2 tbsp oil. Roll each ball to a 33cm round about 5mm thick, lift it into a tin and press it into the base and about 3-4cm up the sides. The oil fries the outside of the crust as it bakes, making it crisp and golden.

steps.title: Fill in reverse
steps.text: Lay half the mozzarella over each base, spread half the sauce over the cheese right to the crust, and sprinkle each with half the Parmesan. Putting the cheese underneath protects it from burning during the long bake.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.text: Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges. Rest in the tins for 10 minutes so the cheese sets, then loosen with the spatula, lift out and cut each into 6 wedges. Cutting too soon lets the molten cheese run out.

tips: A common mistake is using a thin, watery sauce, which soaks the crust; simmer it until thick and reduced to about 600ml.
Keep the butter very soft but not melted for the layering step, so it spreads easily without tearing the dough.
Avoid loose-based tins, as the oil and butter can leak out during baking.
Slice the mozzarella thinly for even melting under the sauce.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven or a dry frying pan until piping hot (74°C).
